title: Icon, pictogram, symbol, glyph, logo — Image Wiki

rules.rule: An icon is a small functional picture inside an interface that acts as a control the size of a fingertip, requiring a touch target of at least 44 pixels.
rules.evidence: An icon is a small functional picture inside an interface: tap it and something happens. Carbon draws its interface icons on 16-pixel artboards and requires a touch target of 44 pixels or more, which tells you what an icon really is — a control the size of a fingertip.

rules.rule: A pictogram is a larger pictorial sign representing a thing, place, or service in the physical world that must survive being read across a room.
rules.evidence: A pictogram is a pictorial sign that stands for a thing, a place or a service in the physical world. It is bigger, it does nothing when touched, and it has to survive being read across a room.

rules.rule: A symbol is conventional meaning assigned rather than depicted, requiring prior knowledge of facts like the red diagonal bar meaning forbidden.
rules.evidence: A symbol is conventional. Its meaning was assigned, not depicted, so it cannot be worked out — only remembered. The red diagonal bar, the recycling triangle, the wheelchair, the biohazard trefoil: every one is a fact you learned.
